Elena — great questions. Short answers up front and runbook below.

- Fallback thresholds: sustained 5xx rate > 3% for 2 consecutive 60s windows OR median latency > 1.8s for 3 consecutive 60s windows on the primary pool.
- Roll-forward vs rollback: a roll-forward is allowed if (1) errors spike but CPU/GPU metadata shows KV warmup in-progress and error rate drops within 10 minutes; (2) we see prefix cache hit rate recovering > 60% within 8 minutes. Rollback if persistent 5xx > 3% after 15 minutes or if downstream traces show persistent model OOMs.

I've attached the runbook we will use and a short smoke checklist. Key notes included under -- KV warmup procedure -- and -- Adaptive routing observation points --.  

[Attachment: runbook_v1.4.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: adaptive-routing-smoke.csv (text/csv)]

- 06:00 — Pre-cutover canary: 5m of light production traffic to new network path + KV prime.
- 06:10 — Evaluate canary metrics, manual hold at 06:15 if any 5xx or latency regression.
- 06:20 — Gradual ramp to 25% production traffic for 20m with continuous KV priming.
- 06:45 — If metrics look good, proceed to 100% by 07:10 with staggered agent restarts.
